chapter: New Orleans bands, players and halls
title: Who first picked the string bass; Foster's bass in Los Angeles and New York
summary: Foster counters claims of who invented picking bass and describes being the only string bass in L.A. in 1922 and how New York players took it up.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: John Veeam rockin' his head. He was doing that years and years ago, see? There's that some bass player from Los Angeles. See, he invented picking string bass. So I wanted to know how old he was, see? He was a young man. So I said, well, I said, Steve Brown from New Orleans was president of Detroit Local, played rock in New Orleans, played tuba and string bass for years. He was picking, and I said, well before him, I said, Jimmy Johnson with the bowling band was picking bass way back in the 18-something and I had some guys way before him. I said, because they had a band out of Donovan, the bass player, he played violin and bass, Henri Baltimore.
Oh, I heard of him, too.

Yeah. See? Did he pick the bass? He was picking, picking, picking, wasn't slapping, just picking. Picking it. Oh, yes. See? So, so, they can't, they can't give those, those guys credit. But when I come, when I went around New York, when I left Los Angeles, even in L.A., in 22, there wasn't no string bass out here but me and Montuti. See, nobody didn't pay no attention to Montuti. Didn't start to pay attention to Montuti until I come out here with the Ory band. After I went, Ory went with the black and tan band, or Montuti went black with the tan band, Ory sent for me, you know what I played. Then they started to pay attention to the string bass. Then when I went to New York, I was ashamed to carry the bass because people used to look at it and laugh at me. They were blocked. All they see was string. Then every bass player, what was it, New York player, and tuba and cellos was at my house. That's what he taught me how to read. See? You come, you come, I'll make you play the lessons on the tuba for me. Now when you leave, I'll play that lesson on the string bass for Michael when he come in next. That's right.
And in the next three years, you didn't see nothing much string bass, no tubas. And all them $400 and $500 tubas, you could see them all around that hallway. People didn't want them.
